observations: All 160 sequential, 160 one-process threaded, and 160 process-isolated geometry/STEP jobs completed without worker failure or timeout and produced valid read-back B-reps.
The sequential control had zero configuration mismatches.

The one-process threaded run had 10 of 160 configuration mismatches. The observed mismatch was serialized STEP uncertainty/tolerance; schema/unit selection and writer-local shape-fix tolerance remained correct in the measured records.
The process-isolated run had zero configuration mismatches across 160 attempts.
Conflicting callers of BOPAlgo_Options::SetParallelMode observed another thread's process-global value in 6505 of 16000 set/yield/read attempts.
The shared immutable stock shape retained its measured volume under the tested non-destructive threaded workload. This is not evidence that concurrent mutation is safe.

At this campaign size, eight process-isolated workers completed the equal 160-attempt workload about 40.7 ms slower than one-process threads, approximately 3.18 percent wall-time overhead, while eliminating the observed STEP tolerance cross-talk.

architecture_input.decision: Retain process-isolated OCCT workers as the founding scheduler-level concurrency boundary.
architecture_input.threading: Allow thread-level parallelism inside an isolated worker only for explicitly qualified APIs with job-local or immutable ownership and without concurrent mutation of process-global configuration.
architecture_input.step: Prefer explicit DESTEP_Parameters and job-local sessions/writers, but do not infer full isolation from those APIs: the measured STEP writer tolerance path crossed jobs under same-process concurrency.
architecture_input.global_state: Do not multiplex conflicting Interface_Static or BOPAlgo_Options process-global settings across jobs in one address space.
architecture_input.topology: Read-only shared TopoDS_Shape/TShape ownership passed this narrow non-destructive workload; concurrent mutation remains unqualified.

remaining_unknowns: ThreadSanitizer qualification of the used OCCT subset.
All legacy Interface_Static consumers and other lazy/static caches outside the measured surfaces.
Long-duration soak, cancellation, allocator pressure, signals, and malformed STEP inputs.
Production worker-pool startup and recycling overhead under realistic mixed workloads.
